name: Init Publish Rules for Both Hosts

pr.title: Have init allow both publish commands for Claude Code and Codex, inside a repository or not
pr.head: ddab4ef891f323ed07db937a1be5c9ab7106e547

summary: project init used to add one Claude Code allow rule, for project review publish, and failed outside a Git repository. Codex's approval reviewer then refused project summary publish twice as sending repository content to another host, so summaries stopped at local previews.

This change covers both publish commands on both hosts. The user's Claude Code settings gain Bash(project summary publish *) beside the review rule. Where Codex's configuration directory already exists, init writes a Projector-owned rules/projector.rules holding one prefix_rule that allows project review publish and project summary publish. Outside a repository, init now sets up only those two user-level files and exits 0.
The terminal, --publish-rule, --no-publish-rule and review.publish_rule decide both hosts together. Without a terminal, init only reports each file as kept and says how to add the rules.

cards.title: What the review found at this head
cards.html:
• Open: src/projector/cli.py:1276. Outside a repository without a terminal, init says it set up the rules though both files were only reported as kept.
  • Open: docs/cli.md:84. Line 33 still says init manages one of your files. Line 117 points at Codex keep reasons that the Codex entry never names.
  • Checked: codex execpolicy check on the written file allows exactly the two publish commands. Merging keeps the user's rules and their order, and a second run reports unchanged.

groups.title: The rules and the two writers
groups.kicker: What init writes into each host's user settings, and how it handles a file it cannot use
intro: RULES replaces the single RULE with both Claude Code patterns. CODEX_RULES is the whole Codex file. Codex loads every *.rules file in its rules/ directory and saves the approvals a person grants to default.rules. So Projector owns projector.rules and rewrites it whole rather than merging into the user's file.

allow_publish now returns a list: the Claude Code action from allow_in_claude, plus a Codex action from allow_in_codex when codex_home() ($CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex) is a directory. Both writers write through symlinks with write_through, and keep a file they cannot read or write, with a note.
concepts: A Codex prefix_rule with decision = "allow" runs the matched command without prompting and outside Codex's sandbox.
Codex counts as installed only when its configuration directory exists, so init never creates one.

checks.text: allow_in_claude appends only the missing rules, so a file holding only the review rule gains the summary rule and keeps the user's order.
The pattern ["project", ["review", "summary"], "publish"] matches the two publish commands and nothing else, such as project summary init or project site serve.
allow_in_codex reports unchanged only when the file is byte-for-byte CODEX_RULES, so a hand edit is overwritten and reported updated.

files.note: The two rule constants, codex_home, and the new allow_in_codex beside the renamed allow_in_claude.

groups.title: One decision, and init outside a repository
groups.kicker: How the CLI decides the rules once for both hosts, and what init does where there is no repository
intro: publish_rule_mode lifts the inline decision out of run so both paths share it. It returns "add", "report", or None.

run now catches the EnvironmentError that discover_git_root raises, for init only, and hands off to init_permissions_only. That path refuses --site and --url with exit 2, writes only the user's rules files, and reports them. emit_files gains readme=False, so that path's JSON lists only files, with no top-level action or path describing a projects README that does not exist.
concepts: In a repository, the top-level action and path in --json still describe the projects README, for older consumers.

checks.text: src/projector/cli.py:1276: done is chosen from files being non-empty. In report mode both files are kept and nothing is written, yet stderr says init set up only the permission rules. Choose the wording from what init actually did.
Only init falls through to init_permissions_only; every other command still raises on a missing repository.
In a repository, publish_rule_mode still runs before any file is written, so a bad review.publish_rule refuses first.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Every test that reaches the writers runs under a temporary HOME
intro: RepositoryTestCase already pointed HOME at a temporary directory and unset CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. It now also unsets CODEX_HOME, so a real Codex configuration cannot be reached. New tests cover the summary rule joining an existing review rule; the Codex file created, unchanged, and restored; CODEX_HOME; no Codex directory; report mode; init outside a repository; and a codex execpolicy check of the rule, which is skipped where codex is missing.

checks.text: The Codex writer's kept branches (not UTF-8, unreadable, rules not a directory, unwritable) and its symlink write-through have no tests, unlike the Claude writer's.

groups.title: Documentation and skills
groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the two skills that tell an agent what to do when a publish is refused
intro: docs/cli.md describes the second Claude Code rule, the Codex rules file, and init outside a repository. summarize-pr gains the instruction review-pr already had: when a host refuses publish, do not retry it in another form, and ask the user to run project init in a terminal or to run publish themselves. review-pr now mentions the Codex rules too.

checks.text: docs/cli.md:84: line 33 still says init manages one of your files, and line 117 says the Codex rules file is kept "for the reasons their entries above name", but the Codex entry names none.
Both skills say init adds the rules only for a person at a terminal, so an agent never runs it to add them.
